name: Change Management Plan
purpose: The change management plan is a component of the project management plan and describes how change is managed on the project. It covers the structure and membership of the change control board, definitions of change, and the process from submitting a change request to its disposition. It is developed once and is not usually changed.

elements.guidance: Describe the degree of change control and how change control integrates with other aspects of project management.
Four definitions, one for each change type below; each says where the line is between a change that must go through change control and an ordinary update.
Define a schedule change versus a schedule revision, and say when a schedule variance must go through change control to be re-baselined.
Define a budget change versus a budget update, and say when a budget variance must go through change control to be re-baselined.
Define a scope change versus progressive elaboration, and say when a scope variance must go through change control to be re-baselined.

elements.element: Definitions of change: Project Document Change
elements.guidance: Say when updates to project management documents or other project documents must go through change control to be re-baselined.
The board's members, with four attributes per member (below).
The person's position on the change control board.
The responsibilities and activities required of the role.
The authority level for approving or rejecting changes.
The four steps below, each described in prose.

elements.element: Change control process: Change request submittal
elements.guidance: Describe how change requests are submitted, including who receives them and any special forms, policies or procedures.

elements.element: Change control process: Change request tracking
elements.guidance: Describe how requests are tracked from submittal to final disposition.

elements.element: Change control process: Change request review
elements.guidance: Describe how requests are reviewed, including analysis of the impact on project objectives such as schedule, scope and cost.

elements.element: Change control process: Change request outcome
elements.guidance: Describe the possible outcomes, such as accept, defer or reject. Table 2.2 calls this row Change request outcome; the blank form prints Change request disposition.

tailoring: If only a few product components or project documents need configuration management, change management and configuration management can be combined into one plan.

The rigor and structure of the plan should reflect the product development approach: rigorous change management for predictive approaches; for adaptive approaches the plan should allow for evolving scope.
agile_or_adaptive: For adaptive approaches the change management plan should allow for evolving scope; rigorous change management suits predictive approaches (Tailoring Tips, PDF page 36, printed page 25).
